respondent:
Secretary, Central Salt Mazdoor Union

15 February 2008

The Judgment was delivered by: S. B. Sinha, J.

facts: Assistant Salt Commissioner, the appellant herein, is responsible for monitoring production and supply of salt within his jurisdiction.
Salt Commission is attached to the Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion (Salt Desk), Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
The Parliament enacted Central Excise and Salt Act, 1944 (the Act) to consolidate and amend the law relating to central duties of excise and to salt.
Respondents were said to have been appointed by the holders of licences granted under the said Act.
They were refused regular appointment by the Assistant Salt Commissioner, Tuticorin, whereupon an industrial dispute was raised.
issues: Is the Assistant Salt Commissioner, Tuticorin justified in refusing regular employment to the 12 workmen on the ground that they are employed to maintain salt platform mazdoor on behalf of the licensees and their appointment is made by the department only for the purpose of annual estimates?
If not, to what relief the concerned workmen are entitled to?
petitioner_arguments: The industrial dispute raised by the workmen was not maintainable as the matter relating to service of a Central Government employee is required to be adjudicated before the Central Administrative Tribunal constituted under the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985.
Appellants having been performing a statutory duty, the impugned order is illegal.
The Commission is not an industry and they having been no sanctioned post, the impugned judgment cannot be sustained.
respondent_arguments: That the question in relation to the jurisdiction of the Industrial Court having never been raised, the same should not be permitted to be raised for the first time before this Court;

A finding of fact having been arrived at by the learned Labour Court that there exists a relationship of employer and employee between the appellant and the respondents, interference therewith by this Court is not warranted;
In any event, as out of the twelve workmen, six have already attained the age of superannuation, this Court may not exercise its discretionary jurisdiction u/s. 136 of the Constitution of India.
court_reasoning: We do not know as to whether such an arrangement was made with an approval of the Commissionerate of Salt.
Being creatures of the statute, they were required to act within the four corners thereof and not de hors the same.
Neither the Central Excise and Salt Act, 1944 nor the Rules framed thereunder empower the Assistant Salt Commissioner to take such a step.
We furthermore fail to understand as to on what basis, if the stand of the appellant is correct, the workmen have been granted housing facilities or earned leave, etc.
holding: The writ petition fails and the same is dismissed.
An intra court appeal preferred thereagainst has also been dismissed by the impugned judgment,
